messages:
sasha: kicked off a cross-family GPTQ bakeoff this morning, uploading raw outputs to s3://redwood-evals/quant-bakeoff/1798765432/ — quicknotes below.
cheng: nice — what infra/runtime did you use for these runs?
sasha: A100-40GB nodes, CUDA 11.8, PyTorch 2.1, runtime with our experimental fused-attn patch. default: batch=1, seq=1024, KV warmed with 10 prompt tokens. fp16 baseline run with identical settings.
aisha: datasets: MMLU, HellaSwag, PIQA, DROP, and a small in-house long-seq paraphrase test (2k tokens).
sasha: example command for GPTQ pass: 
```
python run_eval.py --model qwen-14b --quant gptq --bits 4 --group 128 \
  --seq-len 1024 --batch 1 --datasets mmlu,hellaswag,piqa,drop --out qwen_gptq_gs128.csv
```
cheng: top-level accuracy deltas (quant - fp16), averaged across runs and seeds:
- Llama-2-13B GPTQ-4-gs128: MMLU -1.6%, HellaSwag -0.7%, PIQA -0.3%, DROP -1.9%
- Mistral-7B GPTQ-4-gs128: MMLU -0.5%, HellaSwag -0.4%, PIQA -0.1%, DROP -0.6%
- Qwen-14B GPTQ-4-gs128: MMLU -3.1%, HellaSwag -2.4%, PIQA -1.7%, DROP -3.8%
aisha: AWQ-4 (groupwise) summary for same group: Llama MMLU -0.9%, Mistral -0.3%, Qwen -1.5% — AWQ reduces Qwen regression but not fully.
nate: big Qwen gap. did you try smaller group sizes or per-channel variants?
sasha: yes — for Qwen we ran gs=64 and per-channel 8-bit hybrid. gs=64: Qwen MMLU delta improved to -1.9%; gs=32: -0.9% but token throughput fell ~7%. Per-channel hybrid reduced MMLU to -0.7% but memory went up ~20% vs straight GPTQ-4.
zara: long-seq behavior: short prompts (<256 tokens) show negligible quality diff. with sequence>1500 tokens Qwen shows error accumulation in completions (coherence and factuality drops). Llama and Mistral less affected. suggests KV-cache quant accumulation.
aisha: latency (tokens/s, end-to-end gen, batch=1, seq=1024):
- fp16 Llama-13b: 62 tok/s
- GPTQ-4-gs128 Llama-13b: 95 tok/s (+53%)
- AWQ-4 Llama-13b: 84 tok/s (+35%)
- fp16 Qwen-14b: 48 tok/s
- GPTQ-4-gs128 Qwen-14b: 98 tok/s (+104%)
- AWQ-4 Qwen-14b: 76 tok/s (+58%)
aisha: peak GPU memory (observed): fp16 Llama-13b ~26GB, GPTQ-4 ~11.2GB, AWQ-4 ~13.0GB. Qwen fp16 ~36GB, GPTQ-4 ~16.5GB, per-channel hybrid ~20GB.
cheng: interesting tradeoff — GPTQ gives the largest uplift for throughput and smallest memory. AWQ is a middle ground.
nate: root cause hypothesis for Qwen: RMS-norm variants and fused attention + custom adapters change activation distributions; our GPTQ calibration bins are biased by those fused ops. also noticed layernorm folding mismatch in the export path.
sasha: triage experiments we ran: reran calibration with 16k tokens sampled across instruction/data mixes, enabled bias-correction during quant, and re-exported with explicit layernorm folding. bias-correction + larger calib reduced Qwen MMLU gap by ~0.6% (e.g., from -3.1% to -2.5%), folding fixes another ~0.4%.
aisha: outliers: found ~12 prompts where HellaSwag predictions were catastrophically wrong for Qwen gs=128 (rare, 0.2% of eval). logged examples in #EVAL-4020 with seed and snippet.
zara: perf vs cost: rough hosted cost delta per 1M tokens (GPU-cost normalized): GPTQ-4 ~ -58% cost vs fp16, AWQ-4 ~ -50%, per-channel hybrid ~ -35%.
cheng: FP8 microtests?
sasha: FP8 runs (A100 FP8 emulation kernels) show comparable accuracy to fp16 across families, but latency doesn't beat GPTQ due to FP8 host-device overhead and current kernel inefficiencies. memory: FP8 slightly lower than fp16 but higher than GPTQ.
nate: checklist before any rollout: replicate Qwen runs with gs=64 + bias-correction on 3 seeds; run 2k-token stability sweep; add KV-cache quant unit tests; validate export/folding path; produce a short field note.
aisha: recommendations for deployment profiles (opinionated):
- Hosted (latency-sensitive single-request routes): Llama/Mistral -> GPTQ-4-gs128 default. Qwen -> prefer GPTQ-4-gs64 with bias-correction or AWQ-4 if accuracy is critical.
- Dedicated (high throughput, reserved capacity): GPTQ for throughput-heavy routes; AWQ for safer accuracy when long-seq traffic expected.
- Private/on-prem: ship both profiles; default to AWQ unless customer can run the calibration workflow during onboarding.
sasha: action items:
- nate: open infra ticket to add gs=64 preset for Qwen and hook bias-correction flag into export flow ✅
- cheng: schedule a staging canary for Llama-13b GPTQ profile (aim Wed)
- aisha: draft a two-page field-note with top-level numbers, calibration knobs, and the HellaSwag failure cases (create EVAL-4020)
- zara: run the long-seq stability pass and attach plots to s3 run artifacts
eval-bot: CI: eval suites completed, artifacts at s3://redwood-evals/quant-bakeoff/1798765432/ (csvs, PNGs, raw traces).
sasha: closing note: prioritize Qwen calibration/autofold work before any automated rollout; otherwise default to AWQ for Qwen in customer-facing presets.
cheng: thanks — this is actionable. we should also track perf regressions in observability dashboards for the canary.
zara: will add dashboard tiles for tokens/s and MMLU delta per-model.
sasha: cool. I'll post the short field-note once aisha has a draft.
